rules.description: Modules must not form circular dependencies.
rules.what: Detects import cycles across the module dependency graph.
rules.why: Cycles couple modules, block refactoring, and hide design flaws.

rules.description: Every module should be reachable from the graph.
rules.what: Flags modules that nothing imports (excluding entrypoints).
rules.why: Orphan modules are usually dead code or a missing wiring.

rules.description: Higher layers may import lower layers, never the reverse.
rules.what: Enforces a declared layer order over path globs.
rules.why: Layering keeps dependencies flowing one direction so the core stays clean.

rules.description: Declared module pairs must never depend on each other.
rules.what: Flags any import that matches a forbidden from/to path pair.
rules.why: Explicit forbidden edges protect boundaries from accidental coupling.

rules.description: Declared entrypoints must exist on disk.
rules.what: Verifies each declared entrypoint path is present.
rules.why: A missing entrypoint means the declared architecture is already wrong.

rules.description: Capabilities must be abstracted into canonical patterns rather than rebuilt.
rules.what: Blocks direct usage of restricted libraries, primitives, and symbols outside declared canonical modules.
rules.why: Stops agents and developers from rebuilding the wheel instead of abstracting and reusing shared code.

rules.description: Core functions and classes should be defined once and reused.
rules.what: Flags duplicate function and class names defined across multiple modules.
rules.why: Duplicate symbols across feature modules signal copy-pasting instead of abstraction.

rules.description: Similar function implementation shapes should be reviewed for a shared abstraction.
rules.what: Finds cross-module functions with highly similar normalized control, operator, and call patterns.
rules.why: Renamed copy-paste can evade duplicate symbol-name checks while rebuilding the same capability.

rules.description: Governed source files must have companion .synthetic files defining user workflows.
rules.what: Verifies that source files have a sibling .synthetic file declaring user-journey workflows.
rules.why: Enforces intentional behavioral documentation and enables user-journey governance.

rules.description: User workflows must not duplicate intent and step sequences across parallel implementations.
rules.what: Detects duplicate or near-duplicate user workflow patterns across different modules.
rules.why: Prevents parallel user flows and fragmented customer journeys.

rules.description: Declared .synthetic workflow steps must align with code AST and token reality.
rules.what: Cross-checks external:* and emit:* steps and validates that declared orchestrators are not empty stubs.
rules.why: Prevents synthetic drift where .synthetic companion files become stale or hallucinated.
